story.title: Prince Harry and Meghan Plan Return to the UK with Their Children
story.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are set to return to the United Kingdom after living in the US for over six years. Reports indicate that they will reside in a private home outside London, and their children are expected to enroll in a British school. Buckingham Palace has confirmed the couple's move back to the UK.

explore_lenses.label: Is this a full-time move or an extended stay?
explore_lenses.title: The duration and arrangements remain unclear
explore_lenses.summary: The reporting describes an extended UK stay beginning in fall 2026, rather than a clearly confirmed permanent relocation. School enrollment points to a near-term move, but the family is reportedly retaining homes outside Britain.

claims.text: AP reported on August 19 that the Sussexes planned an extended UK stay starting in fall 2026, with Archie and Lilibet expected to begin British school in September; the details came from a person close to the couple who was not authorized to speak publicly.
The same AP report said the family planned to live in a private, non-royal residence outside London while keeping their Montecito home and a Portuguese vacation property.

Buckingham Palace did not publicly comment on the reported move, citing its policy not to comment on speculation involving non-working royals; a representative for Harry and Meghan also declined comment, AP reported.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: There is no public confirmation in the consulted reporting of a permanent move, the address, or how long the family will remain in Britain.

explore_lenses.label: Why won't they resume royal duties?
explore_lenses.title: A UK base would not restore their royal role
explore_lenses.summary: Living in Britain would not reverse the formal settlement reached after the couple stepped back from senior royal work. Their reported plan is to remain financially independent and conduct private commercial and charitable work.

claims.text: Buckingham Palace confirmed in February 2021 that Harry and Meghan would not return as working members of the Royal Family and that royal duties and associated honorary appointments could not continue after their departure.

AP reported that the planned return would not include a resumption of working-royal roles; it said Meghan was expected to continue leading her As Ever business and Harry could spend more time with his UK-based charities.
The 2021 palace statement framed the rule as institutional: stepping away from royal work meant relinquishing the responsibilities and duties connected to public service.

explore_lenses.label: Will security and family ties shape the return?
explore_lenses.title: Security remains case-by-case as relations thaw
explore_lenses.summary: The move follows recent signs of contact with King Charles III, but it also reopens a long-running dispute over Harry's UK protection. Courts upheld a system under which his protection is assessed according to the circumstances of each visit rather than automatically restored.

claims.text: In May 2025, the Court of Appeal rejected Harry's challenge to the protection arrangements, holding that RAVEC could use bespoke, case-by-case arrangements for his UK visits and describing that approach as sensible.

Harry's counsel, Shaheed Fatima KC, argued that the process had given him inferior treatment and that the risks to him remained significant; the court said those concerns did not establish a legal basis to overturn the decision.

In July 2026, Buckingham Palace confirmed that Charles and Queen Camilla met Harry, Meghan, Archie and Lilibet at Highgrove House, their first such family meeting in years, amid efforts to repair the rift.
AP characterized the extended stay as a development that could help repair family relations, but said the motive for the return was not clear and Harry declined to discuss it.

story_report.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are reportedly planning an extended stay in Britain beginning in fall 2026, after more than six years in the United States. Archie and Lilibet are expected to start British school in September, while the family would live in a private, non-royal residence outside London and retain homes in Montecito and Portugal. The reported plans would return the family to the UK without restoring Harry and Meghan to working-royal duties.

sections.heading: Royal roles remain unchanged
sections.body: The reported return would not alter the arrangement set out by Buckingham Palace in February 2021, when it said the couple would not return as working members of the Royal Family. The palace said that stepping away from royal work meant relinquishing the responsibilities, duties and honorary appointments associated with public service. AP reported that Meghan was expected to continue leading her As Ever business, while Harry could spend more time with his UK-based charities.

sections.heading: Security arrangements shape UK visits
sections.body: Harry's security arrangements remain a practical issue for any longer stay. In May 2025, the Court of Appeal rejected his challenge to the protection system, ruling that the body responsible could use bespoke, case-by-case arrangements for his UK visits. Harry's lawyer had argued that he received inferior treatment and continued to face significant risks, but the court found no legal basis to overturn the decision.

sections.heading: Family contact may increase
sections.body: Buckingham Palace confirmed in July 2026 that King Charles and Queen Camilla met Harry, Meghan, Archie and Lilibet at Highgrove House, in what AP described as the first such family meeting in years. AP said the extended stay could aid efforts to repair family relations, although it reported that the reason for the planned return was unclear and that Harry declined to discuss it.

unresolved.text: Neither Buckingham Palace nor a representative for Harry and Meghan publicly confirmed the reported plans. The reporting does not establish whether the stay would be permanent, the family’s address, or its duration.
No change to the couple's 2021 non-working-royal arrangement has been announced, and the future security plan and extent of contact with other royals have not been made public.

related_stories.title: Trump Indicates Willingness to Meet Kim Jong-un, Cites Nuclear Arsenal Size
related_stories.summary: Trump expressed his willingness to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, stating, 'I get along with him.' He also disclosed that North Korea possesses 57 nuclear weapons, marking the first time a U.S. official has publicly provided a specific number regarding the country's nuclear arsenal.

related_stories.title: UAE Suspends All Trade and Financial Transactions with Iran
related_stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has announced a complete halt to all trade and financial dealings with Iran following the launch of two ballistic missiles from Iran towards the UAE. This decision marks a significant shift in relations, as the UAE has been Iran's most important regional trading partner. The crude oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz has also reportedly decreased to less than a quarter of pre-war levels.
